title: 1st Truth The Testimony Of Createdness In The Cosmos

questions.question: Why does the passage say things cannot make one another forever in a chain?
questions.answer: Because that idea does not make sense and cannot go on without an end.

questions.question: After rejecting that endless chain, what kind of Being must exist?
questions.answer: A Being who always exists and made everything else.

questions.question: What does the passage say about anything other than that Being?
questions.answer: Everything else is made and depends on Him.

questions.question: What big season example shows that created things do not last forever?
questions.answer: In fall, many plants and little animals die.

questions.question: About how many kinds of living things are said to die in that season?
questions.answer: Hundreds of thousands of kinds.

questions.question: Is that dying described as messy or well-arranged?
questions.answer: It is described as well-arranged.

questions.question: What small things are left behind after many living things die?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs.

questions.question: What happens to those seeds and eggs later?
questions.answer: In spring, they help new life come back.

questions.question: What do the seeds and eggs show about Allah’s care?
questions.answer: They show His mercy, wisdom, power, and knowledge.

questions.question: Before they die, what do the living things pass on in a special way?
questions.answer: They leave what is like their life record and plan in the seeds and eggs.

questions.question: Who keeps those seeds and eggs safe?
questions.answer: Allah, the Glorious Preserver.

questions.question: What false idea does the passage argue against at the start?
questions.answer: That things can keep causing one another forever.

questions.question: If that false idea is wrong, what does that help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove that there must be one Necessary Existent.

questions.question: Can there be another one exactly like Him?
questions.answer: No. No equal like Him can exist.

questions.question: What does the passage call the rest of creation compared with Him?
questions.answer: It says all other things are dependent and created.

questions.question: Where can we clearly see signs of created things with our own eyes?
questions.answer: We can see them in the world during autumn.

questions.question: What happens to the living world in autumn?
questions.answer: A whole world of living things seems to die.

questions.question: Are only a few plants and animals mentioned, or very many?
questions.answer: Very many are mentioned.

questions.question: How is the death of these living things described?
questions.answer: It is careful, ordered, and disciplined.

questions.question: Why are seeds and eggs important in the passage?
questions.answer: They carry the way for life to begin again in spring.

questions.question: What do these new springtime lives remind us of?
questions.answer: They remind us of rising again and coming back to life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the idea that things create each other?
questions.answer: It says that idea is impossible.

questions.question: Why is an endless line of causes not accepted here?
questions.answer: Because it would never truly explain where things began.

questions.question: So who must be behind creation?
questions.answer: Allah, the One who must exist.

questions.question: What special difference is there between Allah and all other things in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah must exist, but everything else is created and dependent.

questions.question: What part of the year is used as proof that the world changes?
questions.answer: Autumn.

questions.question: What happens to many plants and tiny animals then?
questions.answer: They die.

questions.question: How does the passage describe each member of those species?
questions.answer: Each one is like a little world by itself.

questions.question: What shows that their death is not without purpose?
questions.answer: They leave seeds and eggs behind for new life.

questions.question: What season brings the new life out again?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: Which beautiful qualities of Allah are shown by this return of life?
questions.answer: His mercy, wisdom, power, and knowledge.

questions.question: What is trusted into seeds and eggs before death?
questions.answer: What is like a record of deeds and a plan for living.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage reach after saying creatures cannot keep making other creatures?
questions.answer: There must be One eternal Maker.

questions.question: Does the passage present that Maker as one among many, or as unique?
questions.answer: As unique.

questions.question: What word best fits things other than that Maker: independent or dependent?
questions.answer: Dependent.

questions.question: What large sign of createdness can people watch in nature?
questions.answer: The dying of much life in autumn.

questions.question: Is only one kind of living thing said to die, or many kinds?
questions.answer: Many kinds.

questions.question: What two small carriers of future life are named?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs.

questions.question: What do those small carriers help bring in spring?
questions.answer: They help bring rebirth and new life.

questions.question: Why is that return of life called wondrous in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows amazing mercy, wisdom, power, and knowledge.

questions.question: What is compared to a life record and plan that gets passed on?
questions.answer: What is placed into the seeds and eggs.

questions.question: Under whose guarding care are those things left?
questions.answer: Under Allah’s guarding care.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what idea is called absurd?
questions.answer: The idea that causes keep going back forever and things make each other.

questions.question: What must be true instead?
questions.answer: There must be One who necessarily exists.

questions.question: What does the passage say about having another one like Him?
questions.answer: That cannot happen.

questions.question: According to the passage, what are all other things like?
questions.answer: They are created beings.

questions.question: How far does the sign of createdness spread in the passage?
questions.answer: Through the whole universe.

questions.question: Can all of those signs be seen with the eyes?
questions.answer: No. Some are seen by the mind.

questions.question: Which signs are easy to see with our eyes?
questions.answer: The dying of many living things in autumn.

questions.question: What is surprising about that death?
questions.answer: It happens in an ordered and controlled way.

questions.question: What is left behind so life can continue?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs are left behind.

questions.question: What do those seeds and eggs become part of in spring?
questions.answer: The coming back of living things.

questions.question: What do the dying creatures seem to hand over before they die?
questions.answer: What is like their record and their plan.

questions.question: What kind of proof is mentioned for the truth in this passage: weak proof or strong proof?
questions.answer: Strong proof.

questions.question: What truth is being strongly proven at the start?
questions.answer: That a Necessary Existent must exist.

questions.question: Why does the passage say created things cannot be the final answer?
questions.answer: Because they cannot keep creating one another without an end.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s uniqueness?
questions.answer: No one can be equal to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the rest of the universe?
questions.answer: It is made by Allah and depends on Him.

questions.question: What yearly event helps us notice that the world does not stay the same?
questions.answer: Autumn brings widespread death in nature.

questions.question: What kinds of living things are named there?
questions.answer: Plants and small animals.

questions.question: Does the passage describe their death as random or purposeful?
questions.answer: Purposeful.

questions.question: What signs of future life remain after they die?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs remain.

questions.question: What season shows life returning again?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: What do we learn from the careful saving of life through seeds and eggs?
questions.answer: Allah preserves and plans for life wisely.
